questions.question: Distinguish between a debit card, a credit card and an EFT.
questions.expected_answer: Debit card: payment taken directly from the holder's own bank account. Credit card: payment made with money borrowed from the bank, to be repaid later, often with interest. EFT: electronic transfer of money from one bank account to another, e.g. salaries, rent.

questions.question: Give two advantages and two risks of electronic banking, and one way to protect yourself.
questions.expected_answer: Advantages (any two): safer than cash; fast and convenient at any time; automatic records; reduces robbery for businesses. Risks (any two): fraud such as phishing and SIM swaps; bank charges and data costs; network or power failures; difficult for some users. Protection: never share PIN/OTP, do not click unknown links, cover the keypad, check statements.

questions.question: Name the four functions of money and give an example of each.
questions.expected_answer: Medium of exchange (buying bread with money); measure of value (comparing prices of two phones); store of value (saving for next year); standard for deferred payment (paying off a fridge in monthly instalments).
